summary:
High-Level Project Summary
OxyNest — Build Life Beyond Earth is a browser-based educational Moon-base management game for children aged 5–12. Players choose buildings, collect resources, run production and complete supply orders while exploring how air, water, food and energy support a settlement. NASA resources provide context for the lunar environment, water ice, space agriculture and life support. Short explanations and an optional guided mode connect player actions with scientific concepts. The project aims to make space-settlement engineering approachable through hands-on play. Gameplay quantities are simplified learning rules, not predictions of real lunar equipment.
details:
OxyNest combines autonomous base management with educational exploration. Players arrange buildings across six plots, collect rocks and ice, upgrade tools and operate production facilities. They decide whether to keep supplies for their crew or deliver them for credits to expand the outpost. Production continues while they explore, allowing different development strategies.

Resource information buttons explain each system before an action. A Knowledge book collects educational cards, while optional guided missions introduce construction, resource processing and environmental challenges. Three age settings adjust mining and guided-task difficulty. The interface supports English and Chinese.

The game uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript without a framework or backend. Illustrations are rendered using inline SVG and CSS. Progress is stored locally in the browser, with no accounts or cloud player analytics.

NASA references inform the educational content. Resource costs, production yields, timers and progression are game-design assumptions. The current playable setting is the Moon; Mars is not a playable destination.
